sections.title: 0. Статус и границы
sections.text:
Этот документ — исполнимый контракт P10. Нельзя менять signatures
`FieldCatalogue::snapshot()` и `AttributeStore::{read,write,loadMany}`. Новые public
типы только additive. Существующие миграции не редактировать. Любое расхождение
между этим текстом и кодом останавливает item и возвращается в design.

sections.title: 1. Инварианты
sections.text:
1. `AttributeId` — UUIDv7 и никогда не выводится из mutable key.
2. `AttributeKey` уникален внутри entity среди effective definitions.
3. Одна identity имеет append-only revisions; published revision не переписывается.
4. Cached catalogue разрешён для чтения, но не является authority для write/DDL.
5. Storage выбирается по entity до обработки patch; внутри record один engine.
6. Любая запись проходит восемь checks в фиксированном порядке (§8).
7. Evolution не удаляет старое представление до backfill verification и grace marker.
8. Outbox append входит в ту же transaction, что и value mutation; payload не несёт values.
9. `corex/attributes` не импортирует `corex/search` и не меняет чужие tables.

sections.title: 2.1 Public additive data types
2.2 Static and module sources
sections.text:
`StaticFieldCatalogue` accepts an immutable `array<string,list<AttributeDefinition>>`.
It needs no DB or modules. Empty entity is a valid empty snapshot, not
`UnavailableAttributes`. `RegistryFieldCatalogue` remains named until P15 and maps
module fields into the same canonical definition.

Module descriptor reads `meta['attribute_id']`. When absent, compatibility mode
creates a deterministic UUIDv5 in a CoreX namespace from `entity + NUL + key`, marks
`meta.legacy_identity=true`, and forbids key change or DB evolution until the owner
pins an explicit UUIDv7. UUIDv5 is only a stable bridge for already shipped keys;
new definitions must supply UUIDv7.

Provider selection is a typed policy object built once from config in the service
provider. Default source is static empty; module source is appended only when both
registries exist. Absence of modules never disables `AttributeStore`.

sections.title: 3. Composite catalogue, DB revisions and cache (P10.3)
3.1 Logical schema — owner gate G-DDL
sections.text:
P10.3 owns one additive migration and the `AttributeTables` additions (D102):

| Table | Key | Required columns | Purpose |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `sys_attribute_definitions` | `(attribute_id, revision)` | UUID `attribute_id`; varchar entity/key/type/lifecycle; bigint revision; booleans required/searchable; jsonb constraints/read_keys/write_keys/index_policy/meta; char(64) definition_hash; timestamps | append-only definition revisions |
| `sys_attribute_key_reservations` | `(entity,key)` | UUID attribute_id; bigint current_revision; varchar role; timestamps | mutable current-key/alias projection, separate from history |
| `sys_attribute_backfills` | UUID `id` | attribute_id; from/to revision; entity; source/target keys; status; cursor_record_id; bigint attempted/changed/failed; char(64) source/target digest nullable; error nullable; timestamps | resumable evolution checkpoint |

Definition history has no `(entity,key)` uniqueness; it is unique only by
`(attribute_id,revision)`. Current uniqueness lives in the reservation table. Publishing a
revision and replacing its complete reservation set is one tenant transaction; rename may
reserve old and new keys to the same attribute but never to different attributes. Foreign key backfill→definition identity is not
used because composite sources may be static/module. No cascade delete. Down drops
only these two new tables and is refused by release procedure after live rows exist.

sections.title: 3.2 Source and merge
sections.text:
`DatabaseFieldCatalogue` reads all latest revisions for entity from the active
tenant connection guarded by `ScopeConnectionGuard`. `CompositeFieldCatalogue`
receives ordered named sources and a `CatalogueConflictPolicy`.

Exactly six distinguishable conflict reasons:

| Reason | Default |
|:--|:--|
| same key, different id | reject |
| same id, different key without migrating alias | reject |
| same id+revision, different type | reject |
| same id+revision, flags/constraints/index differ | reject |
| canonical definitions byte-identical | merge once |
| explicit retirement/deprecation shadow | higher-precedence source wins only when policy names both sources |

No last-write-wins. Source precedence is config, validated unique and complete.
An override record names `(higher,lower,attributeId,allowedDifference)`; wildcard
override is invalid.

sections.title: 3.3 Cache authority
sections.text:
`CachedFieldCatalogue` key includes connection identity, account/workspace/boxed,
entity, source fingerprint and policy version. Cache stores immutable snapshot with
bounded TTL. Definition publish evicts by entity. `AttributeStore::write`,
`SchemaOperations` and backfill resolve the uncached authoritative composite;
`read/loadMany` may use the cached facade. Cache outage falls back to source; malformed
cache fails closed and is evicted.

sections.title: 4. Lifecycle and evolution (P10.4)
sections.text:
Allowed transitions:

```text
draft -> active
active -> deprecated | migrating
deprecated -> active | migrating | retired
migrating -> active | deprecated
retired -> (terminal)
```

Direct active→retired and any transition out of retired are rejected. Rename/type
change uses the same stable id and a new revision:

1. **expand:** publish `migrating`; `readKeys=[new,old]`, `writeKeys=[old,new]`;
2. **sync:** stores write both keys atomically; reads prefer new and compare old;
3. **backfill:** batches order by stable record id; checkpoint advances only after commit;
4. **verify:** require zero missing/divergent values and matching canonical digest;
5. **switch:** publish new active revision with `readKeys=[new,old]`, `writeKeys=[new]`;
6. **grace:** observe fallback counter until owner-defined window reaches zero;
7. **contract:** publish active revision `readKeys=[new]`, then atomically remove the old alias reservation.

Expand, switch and contract update the current-key projection without rewriting immutable history.
The validation fixture retains multiple historical revisions carrying the same entity/key.

Type changes require a registered pure `AttributeValueTransformer` identified in
the definition; absent transformer rejects transition. Backfill is idempotent:
same operation id + record version produces no second mutation. Concurrent user
write locks the record and dual-writes; backfill rechecks record version before
commit and retries conflicts. Abort before switch restores previous active revision;
after switch rollback republishes migrating with reversed key order. Physical drop
is never automatic and remains an explicit verified `SchemaOperations` request.

sections.title: 5. Storage and indexing (P10.5)
6. Query and read semantics
sections.text:
Reads authorise subject and visible fields before loading values. Unknown/hidden
fields are omitted from external bags; internal diagnostics retain reason codes.
During migration, new key wins; if both exist and canonical values differ, read fails
closed for mutation callers and emits a drift diagnostic for read callers. Query
compilation uses only active/deprecated/migrating definitions and declared index policy.

sections.title: 7. Revision precondition
sections.text:
`ValuePatch` receives additive nullable `expectedSchemaHash`. If supplied, it must
equal authoritative snapshot hash. If absent, writes are allowed only to stable
`active` definitions with one read/write key; migrating/deprecated definitions
require the precondition. This preserves existing simple writes while preventing
stale clients from mutating an evolving field.

sections.title: 8. Eight write checks (P10.6)
9. Mutation event and outbox (P10.7)
sections.text:
After a successful non-replay mutation, store creates internal
`AttributeValuesChanged` and translates explicitly to `MessageEnvelope` type
`attributes.values.changed.v1`. The resolved `MessageContractRegistry` is extended,
not replaced.

Payload contains only scope identity, opaque `RecordRef`, record version,
`schemaHash`, sorted changed stable attribute ids and keys, occurred-at and
correlation/causation. It contains no old/new values, labels, constraints or actor PII.
Outbox append occurs inside the same transaction as JSONB/EAV write and token commit.
Write-token replay returns prior result and does not append again.

Consumers are outside attributes. Search projection re-reads current authorised state;
therefore duplicate or out-of-order messages converge to latest record version and no
ordering promise is added beyond D28. No search package symbol appears in attributes.

sections.title: 10. Physical subsystem map (P10.8)
sections.text:
Public `Contracts`, `Data`, `Exceptions` remain. Internal code is grouped:

| Subsystem | Owners |
|:--|:--|
| `Schema` | definitions, catalogues, merge/cache, lifecycle, operations |
| `Values` | stores, validator, write guard, migration read/write |
| `Query` | filter planning and index-aware compilation |
| `Storage` | tables, resolver, connection guard, DB repositories |
| `Integration` | domain event and message translator/registry contribution |
| `Laravel` | registrar/composition only |

P10.8 may move internal FQCNs after consumer sweep. `RegistryFieldCatalogue` rename is
reserved for P15. Public namespaces and config keys remain compatible.

sections.title: 11. Error and security policy
sections.text:
All definition/config errors fail boot or first resolution deterministically. Tenant
connection guard runs before DB read. Logs use stable id and reason, not value. Cache
keys contain hashed scope identity. Constraint regex is bounded and application-owned;
no arbitrary callable/class from DB. Transformer/index identifiers resolve from
declared registries only. Raw SQL identifiers come exclusively from validated tables,
types and generated index names.

sections.title: 12. Final validation recipe
sections.text:
1. Run test DB preflight; prove isolated tenant DB.
2. Run package lint/analyse/test and root `composer test:pg`.
3. Prove module-free static and DB catalogues work with no module bindings.
4. Exercise all six conflict reasons and cache corruption/fallback.
5. Run rename and type change through every state; interrupt/retry each backfill batch.
6. Prove JSONB and EAV dual-write parity, rollback before/after switch, no early drop.
7. Prove resolver rejects per-field/mixed driver and preserves `loadMany` order.
8. Prove dirty cast blocks index; valid index matches query and ordering tie-breaker.
9. Prove each of eight checks independently red and batch atomicity.
10. Prove one mutation/one outbox row, token replay/no second row, no raw values.
11. Run graph/config gates: zero `CoreX\\Search`, no runtime `config()`, no foreign DDL.
12. Compare public API snapshot; only declared additive symbols; write final receipt.

sections.title: 13. Decision map
sections.text:
D50 identity; D51 catalogue/conflicts/cache; D52 evolution; D53 storage/indexing;
D54 eight checks; D55 outbox projection. External evidence: `P10-design-rag.md`.
